displayNameStatus: TBD: placeholder. The owner has not chosen this channel's display name; the show name stands in until he does (CLAUDE.md, Channel 2: 'display name TBD').
scope: Crypto security and AI security news: hacks, exploits, drainers, phishing, key compromises, AI-agent exploits and prompt injection incidents, malicious AI tools, deepfake and voice-clone scams, AI-powered phishing and AI-washing frauds (owner, 2026-11-24).

zooVoice.note: Same decision as content/zoora-ai/channel.json: Kokoro im_nicola for every language. The voice step always gets --voice im_nicola.

sounds.source: Real dog sounds recorded from the owner's dog (clips the owner will supply). No words, no synthesized dog voice, no music, app sounds or other voices.
sounds.placement: As punchlines after Zoo's lines, never over his speech.

badger.jokeCaptions: Only with the owner's OK (e.g. "[Badger: absolutely not]").

segments.name: Cold open
segments.what: The story in one attributed line. onScreen.kicker is "Threat Brief" (no date: the news gate reads on-screen dates as figures). When developing: DEVELOPING on screen (onScreen.title) and said aloud.

segments.name: Rekt Meter
segments.what: What happened: who, when and the reported loss. onScreen.title and onScreen.loss (as the source writes it) with scene.rekt {usd, source}; a second outlet's different figure goes in lossAlt + rekt.alt, never merged. No source states a loss (most AI-security stories): leave out loss and rekt, and the meter is hidden; never $0 or a guess.

segments.name: How it worked
segments.what: The mechanism at concept level, attributed: a 2-5 node diagram (onScreen.nodes, onScreen.links, scene.diagram.nodes). No code, addresses, function names or step lists.

segments.name: Our check
segments.what: The real analysis this video adds (storyboard.analysis): the 30-day tracker comparison, the radar pattern or a fund-flow trace. Required in every daily video.

segments.name: Badger's Red Flag
segments.what: The warning sign a viewer could have spotted (onScreen.flag). Badger's nonverbal reaction carries the joke.

segments.name: Zoo's One Fix
segments.what: One defensive action (onScreen.fix, optional onScreen.detail). Defensive checklists are fine; attack steps are not.

segments.name: Subscribe
segments.what: Subscribe for tomorrow's Threat Brief. With a published evergreen explainer, use the outroEndScreen segment (onScreen.explainer) instead.

segments.name: Badger beat
segments.what: A silent reaction insert: empty narration, minDurationSec 1.2-1.4, badgerBeats [{reaction}].

segments.name: Correction
segments.what: An on-air correction (onScreen.correct, onScreen.date), when one applies; it is also pinned.

dailyShort.condition: Only when a confirmed story exists AND the video adds real analysis. Otherwise publish nothing that day (owner rule: don't publish daily unless each video adds real analysis).

whatWeKnow.when: Major incidents only, on the owner's call. Labelled DEVELOPING until confirmed; corrections pinned.

weeklyLongForm.condition: Must include a fund-flow analysis (news gate rule R7).

evergreenExplainers.what: Every news video links the explainer for its topic once that explainer is published.

cta.noExplainer: No explainer is linked until the topic's evergreen explainer is published (url is null below).

offersNote: None until the owner adds security affiliates (creator-hub/config/offers.json). With offers, the paid-promotion box is ticked and the disclosure is spoken and shown.

containsSyntheticMedia.reason: Clearly animated show with a generic synthetic voice for a fictional host; no realistic depiction of a real person.

publish.paidPromotion: Only when the episode lists offers (offers is empty, so No).
publish.upload: Manual in YouTube Studio by the owner, after APPROVE. The daily tools never upload or call the YouTube API (PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS: do not upload or publish unless the owner requests it separately).
publish.privacyAtUpload: private, then schedule or publish after the checklist

announcer.mode: Dry run unless the owner opts in: the hub announcer posts only with --apply, which the daily passes only through DAILY_ANNOUNCER_CMD (creator-hub/tools/announcer/README.md), and then only for platforms whose credentials are all set, with the video id recorded and the owner's approval on file.
announcer.credentialEnvNote: The names the hub announcer reads (creator-hub/tools/announcer/README.md, 'Credentials'). A platform counts as ready only when every one of its names is set.

threatBrief.mode: Kit DRAFT only, never sent or scheduled by a tool; the owner sends it from Kit. A draft is created only with KIT_API_KEY and THREAT_BRIEF_KIT_FILTER (or --all-subscribers) set, after APPROVE and with the video id recorded. On days with no video, prepare writes a local radar-only draft (out/daily/<date>/threat-brief/).

owner: Label developing stories "developing" and pin corrections.
Don't redraw or speculate about others' material; attribute every fact.
Don't publish daily unless each video adds real analysis.
A strike on either channel endangers both, so accuracy comes first.
accuracy: Every fact traces to a stored source excerpt that contains it.
Loss amounts are "reported by X" and never averaged.
No suspect or individual names, except officials named in law-enforcement or regulator releases.
No exploit how-tos: mechanisms at concept level, with no code, function names or step lists.
